target_customer: Canadian small and medium businesses that pay for payroll, HR and benefits software
problem: Canadian SMBs lacked a modern all in one payroll, HR and benefits platform built for Canadian rules, since popular US tools such as Gusto served only the US.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with per employee payroll and HR fees plus benefits
product_category: Payroll, HR and benefits software for Canada

founders.name: Kevin Kliman
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and CEO on the YC page.

founders.name: Matt Loszak
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and CTO on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Payroll needs correct tax and statutory calculations across Canadian provinces, plus integrations and benefits, which is detailed but standard software work.

defensibility.rationale: Payroll and HR records have high switching costs and Canadian compliance is a barrier, but incumbents such as ADP also served Canada.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were not reported copying it. Employment Hero, an Australian peer, bought Humi in January 2025 for a reported CAD 100 million.

market_need_then: Gusto style modern SMB payroll existed only in the US, leaving Canada with older providers; Humi had over 4,000 business customers by June 2020 according to BetaKit.

branding.domain_note: Used humi.ca; CB Insights lists a former name Humi Payroll.

identity.visual_style: A company blog post on a rebrand exists but could not be opened

brand_strength.rationale: Short memorable name and a recognized Canadian SMB brand, kept by Employment Hero for Quebec; little press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Humi raised a Series A in June 2020 and a Series B in May 2022, serving thousands of Canadian businesses, and sold to Employment Hero in early 2025 for a reported CAD 100 million. It combined a Canada only focus with sticky payroll data, and a regional leader of the same category was the natural buyer. The reported price relative to about CAD 51 million raised is moderate.
notes: Series A was CAD 15 million (12 equity, 3 debt), Series B CAD 31 million (25 equity, 6 debt), total about CAD 51 million; amounts are CAD so amount_usd is left null rather than converted. Acquisition reported at over CAD 100 million (about USD 69.5 million) by trade press, announced 2025-01-08; Employment Hero FAQ says March 2025, so closing date conflicts. No competitor coverage dated near early 2017 was found; Gusto (US only) is mentioned in 2020. Founder list per YC page; other names (Simon Bourgeois, Drew Millington) appear in aggregator and BetaKit as co-founder or co-CEO but are not on the YC page, so not listed. Search results mixed in a few untrusted aggregator pages, ignored.
